purpose: Measure learned traffic avoidance with fixed static-area support, and test closest-approach inputs against equal-capacity zero channels.

evaluation.checkpoint_selection: First saved checkpoint at/above each threshold, within one rollout.
evaluation.classical: Fixed controller with both filters, rerun per row; never tuned.

interpretation: StaticActionProjection and route guidance are unchanged classical support.
Aircraft-to-aircraft traffic filtering is OFF; the learned policy must contribute traffic avoidance.
Each trained policy is compared to its own zero-experience initial checkpoint with identical support.
For each seed the two arms must have identical full initial weights, architecture, environment and training recipe except the 45-channel input mask.
Neither this study nor earlier source/worker/seed configurations alone isolates the effect of adding static filtering. A matched static-off run would be required for that causal claim.
The paired feature-minus-zero change in learning tests predictive input information at fixed network capacity.
All native safety metrics and fixed classical comparisons are retained; clean completion is a development metric, not an official scalar score.
Development stream 20260 has been reused. Reserved streams 20301 and 20302 remain unused until selecting a candidate.
Three training seeds and twenty worlds are a screening experiment, not final competitive evidence.
remaining_experiments: Unseen streams 20301 and 20302 after candidate selection
scheduling: First training row gates the other five on technical completion, not performance; one GPU training task at a time. CPU evaluation has its own allocation. All six rows must be reported.
failure_behavior: Stop on failed checks or incomplete training. Never overwrite existing output.
